_comment: The WinterTC / ECMA-429 Minimum Common API, as a checklist RingServ is
measured against — someone else's list, which is the point. A surface
graded by its own author grades itself generous.
Each entry says what RingServ claims for that name, and tests/js-gates.js
verifies EVERY claim in both directions: `present` must exist and behave,
`absent` must be genuinely absent. A capability that quietly appears later
is as much a defect as one that quietly disappears — this file is what
makes either one fail a build.
Source: the Minimum Common API list published by WinterTC (formerly
WinterCG), read 2026-08-19. Where a name is absent, `why` says so in
terms of this server rather than in terms of the standard.

entries.name: fetch
entries.why: A service reaches another service by NAME through serv.call, and the topology decides where that name lives. A service that hardcodes a URL has made a deployment decision inside application code, which is what placement exists to prevent. Outbound HTTP to the wider internet is a phase-8 decision about egress policy, not an oversight.

entries.name: setInterval
entries.probe: typeof setInterval === 'function' && (() => { try { setInterval(() => {}, 1); return 'usable'; } catch (e) { return 'refused'; } })() === 'usable'
entries.why: Declared so the name is not silently missing, but it THROWS: a request-scoped guest has nowhere to run a repeating timer, and one that survived a request would be a leak with a schedule.

entries.name: crypto.subtle
entries.why: Not yet implemented. Recorded here rather than left to be discovered, because a half-present SubtleCrypto is worse than an absent one.

entries.name: Blob
entries.why: Not yet implemented. The body types a service actually meets are strings and JSON; Blob arrives when a service needs it.

entries.name: CompressionStream
entries.why: Not yet implemented. Streams are phase-8 work: the request path is currently whole-body, so a stream would be a shape with nothing behind it.

entries.name: WebSocket
entries.why: Not yet implemented. The vendored httpz carries a websocket module, so this is a wiring decision rather than a missing capability, and it belongs with the sync work's live channel.

entries.name: require
entries.why: Not part of the standard, and deliberately not provided: it is quickjs-libc's door to the filesystem.

entries.name: process
entries.why: Node's, not the standard's. A guest with no filesystem and no child processes has nothing to put in it.
